description: Flask application (Conduit, a RealWorld-spec blog/social-writing API: articles, comments, tags, favorites, follows) with 6 intentionally vulnerable features, each mapped to a real business capability rather than a generic demo endpoint. Snyk Code detected 4 of 6 (command-injection, insecure-deserialization, path-traversal, ssrf); sql-injection and code-injection were genuine Snyk misses, verified instead by manual source-to-sink trace and a live PoC (see POC.md). Per this batch's realism-first policy, that gap was preserved rather than engineered away.

vulnerabilities.description: The article-search endpoint's `q` parameter is concatenated directly into a raw SQL LIKE clause across title/description/body instead of being passed as a bound parameter. Snyk Code did not report this flow (verified by manual trace and a live PoC, not SARIF) — a genuine scanner miss, not a curation error.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to alter the search query's logic, e.g. bypass the keyword filter entirely and enumerate every article regardless of the supplied term.

vulnerabilities.description: The article-download endpoint joins a request-controlled `filename` parameter onto the article's export directory with no containment check before opening it, allowing `../` sequences to escape the intended per-article folder.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows any reader to read arbitrary files on the server outside the exports folder.

vulnerabilities.description: The article-to-PDF export endpoint passes an optional reader-chosen `label` (falling back to the article title) into a shell command string built for a PDF converter, run with shell=True and no escaping or validation.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to break out of the intended command via shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the server process.

vulnerabilities.description: The "resume my in-progress draft" link restores a parked article draft by base64-decoding and unpickling the unauthenticated `draft` query parameter, with no integrity check.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution by sending any user (or hitting the endpoint directly, since it needs no account or session) a crafted `draft` value.

vulnerabilities.description: The advanced article-filter endpoint evaluates the reader-supplied `expression` with Python's eval(), passing only a local-variable context dict that does not restrict access to builtins. Snyk Code did not report this flow (verified by manual trace and a live PoC, not SARIF) — a genuine scanner miss, not a curation error.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to execute arbitrary Python code, and via __import__, arbitrary OS commands, on the server.

vulnerabilities.description: Updating a profile's `image` field triggers a server-side fetch to confirm the submitted URL actually resolves to an image, with no allowlist or restriction on the target host.
vulnerabilities.vulnerabilityImpact: Allows an attacker to make the server issue arbitrary outbound HTTP requests, including to internal-only services not otherwise reachable from outside the network.
